bifrost: springboard/src/bare/crashlog.rs (panic hook, crash.log, last_exit), springboard/src/shell/diag.rs (CrashEntry), springboard/mcp/src/dev.rs (crash, panic_log), springboard/sdk/src/dispatch.rs (catch_unwind per job), springboard/src/deildu/jobs.rs (catch_unwind with fallback)
summary: Apple's framework is one Objective-C class, NSExceptionHandler, that installs an uncaught-exception handler and lets a delegate decide per exception whether to handle and log it. BifrOSt has no app-facing exception handler API; it captures Rust panics in the system layer (panic hook writes crash.log, unclean exits are noted at the next start) and isolates panics per job in the SDK dispatch and shell job pools.

features.bifrost: springboard/sdk/src/exception_handler.rs (ExceptionHandler::capture, FailureKind::name, Failure::log_line); springboard/src/bare/crashlog.rs (try_append, install, format_panic)
features.note: ExceptionHandler::capture decides a monitored failure and appends its line to the app's crash.log in the shell's format; tested headless in sdk/tests/parity_sdk-rest-08.rs. Gap: the process panic hook stays with the shell, apps cannot install one, and the shell's diagnostics do not read an app's crash.log.

features.note: The failure monitor is tested headless in sdk/tests/parity_sdk-tests-06.rs: the bit layout, log and handle decisions per kind (a_monitored_kind_is_logged...), delegate refusals, the halt mask, and crash record reading with newest-first order and a sixty character signature (crash_records_list_the_newest_crash_first...). Gap: not wired into apps or the shell and not tested on the VM or Midget; diagnostics list crash.log entries and coredumpctl output, and there is no in-app crash reporter API.

start_session and end_session give an app's data directory the shell's start and exit marks; a start with a last_start marker and no last_exit reports the previous run as unclean. Tested headless in springboard/tests/parity_sdk-rest-08.rs and sdk/tests/parity_sdk-rest-08.rs. Gap: the marks are not yet written by an app's own launch path, and the note is not shown to the user.

features.feature: Objective-C exception global string constants and error names
features.apple: NSExceptionHandler global string constants for Objective-C runtime and system exceptions
features.note: Tied to the Objective-C runtime; Rust panics carry a payload string and location, not named exception classes

gaps: No app-facing process panic hook: an app captures failures with sdk exception_handler::ExceptionHandler::capture and lists them with crash_records; the panic hook stays with the shell
Halt mask only: hanging_mask is stored, but no debugger halt is performed; a panic aborts the release build after the hook writes
Panic isolation exists only in SDK dispatch and shell job pools, not for arbitrary app code
